messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — High 5xx rate for /v1/generate in eu-west over the last 3m (error rate 18%). Severity: Sev2. Paging oncall: @oncall-alex. https://metrics.internal/redwood/alerts/1760371200 :rotating_light:
oncall-alex: Acknowledged. I'm on it. Saw some spike in queue latency ~2m ago.
maya-sre: I'm on standby, switching from my handoff. Do we have any customer-facing impact yet?
priya-cs: CS: a few enterprise customers reported elevated latencies and incomplete streams ~10m ago. No escalations to legal yet but one partner (FinLedger) flagged timeouts.
jamie-eng: I see a surge of long-tail requests from eu-west region hitting the high-memory model variant. Traffic pattern looks like a batch job from a single org + a lot of small requests.
oncall-alex: Thanks. Quick status: 1) Error rate up, 2) latency SLOs breaching for lower tiers, 3) rate of KV cache misses increased. Suspect routing/overcommit on a ded pool.
nora-platform: Oncall, do you want temporary throttles or steering? We can flip a smart-routing policy to steer non-prod / low-tier traffic to fallback region or cheaper model.
maya-sre: Let's do minimal-customer-impact route: 1) Apply short rate-limit to free/level-1 plans in eu-west (reduce to 50r/s per org) 2) Steer level-2 and below to eu-central secondary pool for stateless requests 3) For high-cost gen paths, fallback to quantized-variant that preserves semantics. Anyone object?
priya-cs: That plan sounds good. Communicating to FinLedger now with ETA ~15m for mitigation.
nora-platform: I can push routing change. infra-bot, queue me for rollout.
infra-bot: Received. Preparing policy update diff. Will apply with canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% if health OK.
jamie-eng: Adding logs: here's the failing trace snippet we've been seeing:
```
ERROR: decode kv cache miss overflow
model: redwood-large-v1-quant
req_id: 3f9a2b
latency_ms: 12034
stack: /runtime/threadpool.cpp:234
```
Looks like memory pressure causing evictions -> downstream 5xx.
sre-lead-kyle: If memory pressure, steering to a region with lower load is safer than throttling everyone. But throttles reduce blast radius. Combine both: throttle lowest tier + steer medium tier.
oncall-alex: Agreed. Implementing combined approach.
nora-platform: Pushing policy now. Patch:
```
route_policy:
  - match: { region: eu-west, plan_tier: free }
    action: rate_limit
    config: { rps: 50, burst: 100, duration_s: 900 }
  - match: { region: eu-west, plan_tier: level-1 }
    action: steer
    config: { target_region: eu-central, percent: 70 }
  - match: { region: eu-west, plan_tier: level-2 }
    action: steer
    config: { target_region: eu-central, percent: 40 }
  - match: { model_tag: high_mem }
    action: fallback_model
    config: { target_model: redwood-large-v1-quant }
```
Applying canary to 10% of matched traffic now.
infra-bot: Canary applied at 10% — health checks running (5s intervals).
maya-sre: Watching metrics. Error rate dropped from 18% -> 12% at 10% canary. Latency p50 for level-1 still up but trending down.
priya-cs: Customer note: FinLedger acknowledged the mitigation plan, asked for ETA on full fix. I told them we'll have a stable mitigation in ~30m and a postmortem with root cause.
jamie-eng: I pushed a quick temp increase of KV cache size on the eu-west pool to relieve pressure (risk: memory spike). Monitor for OOM. Command: `infractl pool update eu-west --kv-cache-size 1.2x`
infra-bot: KV cache resize submitted, nodes will restart rolling (one at a time). Expect ~2m per node.
maya-sre: Canary to 50% now (nora-platform). Watching for 5xxs.
nora-platform: Canary 50% ok. 5xx at 50% traffic steady at 9%. No OOMs reported so far.
sre-lead-kyle: Good. Proceed to 100% for those steering rules and keep the free-tier rate limit in place for 30m.
oncall-alex: Proceeding to 100%.
infra-bot: Policy rollout to 100% complete.
maya-sre: Post-comparison: error rate back to baseline ~1.2% overall, free-tier still seeing higher latencies but within degraded SLO.
priya-cs: Updated customers: FinLedger says degraded but acceptable; no new support tickets in last 15m.
jamie-eng: I still see a noisy client responsible for the batch job. Can we reach out to the org owner for a scheduled retry window? Might need a long-term throttling rule.
priya-cs: I have the account alias, will reach out after we stabilize.
sre-lead-kyle: Action items: 1) postmortem owner = @maya-sre, 2) routing policy review with platform team for more nuanced cost/latency tiers, 3) follow-up: make fallback_model selection more conservative (QA quantized models against evals).
maya-sre: I'll own the postmortem. Timeline: preliminary within 24h, full root cause and mitigation plan in 72h.
oncall-alex: Handing off to @oncall-alex -> @maya-sre for steady state monitoring. If error rate creeps >5% again, page pager rotation.
priya-cs: I'll send a short customer-facing bulletin to impacted customers mentioning we applied smart-routing mitigations and are doing a full investigation.
jamie-eng: Leaving notes: create a permanent rule to steer non-critical traffic under heavy memory pressure. I'll draft in repo: `infra/route-policies/steering-under-memory-pressure.yaml`
infra-bot: Deploy logs and routing diff stored at: https://internal.redwood/snapshots/1760371200-routing-diff
maya-sre: Closing active mitigation thread. Monitoring for 45m then I'll mark incident as mitigated. Thanks team :white_check_mark:
